title: sail's chart call waits as long as a gate's answer can take, not 120 seconds
intention: sail.py's chart call waits as long as a gate's answer can take: one CHART_TIMEOUT_S (890 s, below the bus socket's 900 s) with a why-comment beside the other timeouts, passed to Ticket.chart; clearance keeps GATE_TIMEOUT_S.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: sail.py:140 chart passes timeout=GATE_TIMEOUT_S (120.0); the tester chart's constrain gate ran many minutes and sail gave up at 120 s while codemother kept going
traces_to: Law 7: a gate that is still running must not be reported as refused by a caller that stopped listening; Law 1: a measured answer (the gate can take minutes) becomes structure, not a retry.
how: Add CHART_TIMEOUT_S = 890.0 beside VERDICT_TIMEOUT_S with the why (the constrain gate runs every proof of the component as instruments), and pass it in chart(). Proof: load sail by path, patch its _ticket to a stub whose chart() records the timeout it is handed, call chart(), assert the recorded timeout is CHART_TIMEOUT_S and at least 890; no live bus.

clauses.claim: chart() hands Ticket.chart the long timeout (CHART_TIMEOUT_S, 890 s), not GATE_TIMEOUT_S

decisions.text: D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; red first.
